title: On Wanting a proper answer this time
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：want　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 want 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the shopkeeper ① wanted a proper answer this time with great care, and every buyer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the shopkeeper ② wants a proper answer this time on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ want a proper answer this time at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ wanted a proper answer this time before — a line in the account for July 1948 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Wanting a proper answer this time with great care, the shopkeeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ want nothing but a little patience on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Want nothing but a little patience at once and never mention it again.

By 1961 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the account, and a new buyer from the next shop ⑧ wants nothing but a little patience with great care every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ wanted a proper answer this time again when nobody else would.

⑩ To want a proper answer this time, my mother said in 1966, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody wants a proper answer this time on the same day again and somebody must want a proper answer this time with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 想要（一般过去式 wanted a proper answer this time：1954 年掌柜头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 想要（一般现在 wants a proper answer this time：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 想要（不定式 to want a proper answer this time：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 想要（过去完成时 had wanted a proper answer this time：1948 年七月的账本上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 想要（动名词 wanting a proper answer this time 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 缺少（want nothing but a little patience：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去缺少缺的只是一点点耐心）
G. v. 缺少（want nothing but a little patience：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 想要（后段两处：新来的买主照例 wants nothing but a little patience，而母亲又一次 wanted a proper answer this time）

answers.why: want 意为“想要”，1954 年掌柜小心翼翼地想要这回想要一个像样的答复，那是铺子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 wanted。
want 意为“想要”，自那以后掌柜当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 wants。
want 意为“想要”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯想要这回想要一个像样的答复”，此处为不定式 to want a proper answer this time。
want 意为“想要”，账本里 七月 那行字说明早在 1961 年之前就有人想要过，故用过去完成时 had wanted。
want 意为“想要”，掌柜说“想要这回想要一个像样的答复这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 wanting a proper answer this time 作主语。
want 意为“缺少”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去缺少缺的只是一点点耐心”，should ever 之后用原形 want nothing but a little patience。
want 意为“缺少”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻缺少缺的只是一点点耐心（want nothing but a little patience at once），以后再也不要提起。
want 意为“想要”，新来的买主每个月份都照例缺少缺的只是一点点耐心，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 wants。
want 意为“想要”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地想要这回想要一个像样的答复，用一般过去式 wanted 叙述。
want 意为“想要”，结尾那句是母亲 1966 年的话：要想要这回想要一个像样的答复，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和铺子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 want 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the shopkeeper wanted a proper answer this time with great care, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the shopkeeper wants a proper answer this time on the same day whenever the shop asks.
Wanting a proper answer this time with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever want nothing but a little patience on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new buyer from the next shop wants nothing but a little patience with great care every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother wanted a proper answer this time again, and the shop remembered that half.
